Perhaps, this 'constructive criticism'...

>You sometimes behave like anarcho-primitivists that Ted was talking about. Some of you, when confronted with an argument against pre-industrial societies do mental gymnastics just to refute this argument no matter how absurd the response is. 

...was just pointing out that in an effort to defend a certain idea, anons end up unnecessarily and even self-harmfully defending an idealized version of some supposed or imagined end result. Please see the last two sentences of paragraph 182 of ISAIF.

>The troubles of primitivism is really not our focus area and I've not seen anyone deny that there's not isolated ''good'' parts in industrial society.

Agree completely. That's why anons must be careful not to come off or seem to potential new-comers as anarcho-primitivists -- specially when most of us surely despise anarcho-communism and all corolaries of it. 

To put it differently:

In other words, by spreading the ideas of Ted, anons might come across as anarcho-primitivists, thus unwittingly generating the very false notion that Ted=anarcho-primitivism, thus ending up defending counter-arguments to anarcho-primitivism when in actual fact ted-anons were never anarcho-primitivists to begin with.
